pk/math.text: Verbally count to 20 by ones
Demonstrate ability to count in sequence
Recognize and name written numerals to 10
Count many kinds of concrete objects and actions up to 10 using one-to-one correspondence
Count as many as 7 things in a scattered configuration with no errors
Recognize, create, and repeat simple patterns
Use a range of strategies (e.g. counting, subtracting, matching) to compare quantity in two sets of objects and describe the comparison with terms, such as more/less, greater than/fewer/equal to
Recognize the attributes of length, area, weight, and capacity of everyday objects, and use appropriate vocabulary (e.g. long, short, light, big, small, wide, narrow)
Compare the attributes of length and weight for two objects including: larger/shorter/same length, heavier/lighter/same, more/less/same
Sort, classify, and serialize objects using attributes, such as color, shape, or size
Use positional words to describe an object's location (e.g. up, down, above, under, inside, outside)
Recognize and name common shapes, their parts and attributes
Create and represent three-dimensional shapes (e.g. ball/sphere, square/box/cube, tube/cylinder using various manipulative materials)
Use the senses and tools, including technology, to gather information, investigate materials, and observe processes and relationships
Make predictions about changes in materials or objects based on past experience
With adult assistance, ask and seek out answers to questions about objects and events
Explore different kinds of matter (e.g. wood, metal, water) and describe by observing properties (e.g. visual, aural, textural)
Explore and describe various actions that can change an object’s motion, such as pulling, pushing, twisting, rolling, and throwing
Investigate, describe, and compare the characteristics that differentiate living from non-living things
Observe and describe ways in which many plants and animals resemble their parents
Describe and anticipate weather changes
Name any celestial object seen in the day or night sky
With adult assistance, recognize examples of technologies (e.g. knife, pencil, computer, pencil sharpener, refrigerator) at home or in the classroom
Observe and describe plants and animals as they go through predictable life cycles
Recognize calendars and simple timelines
Construct and describe simple maps of the classroom or home
Engage in activities that build understanding of words for locations and direction
Identify people's basic needs and explain how they fulfill them
Identify buyers and sellers
Identify one or two workers, and their jobs in the community
Use self-identifying information (e.g. name, age) in situations outside the classroom
Talk about, compare, and explore similarities and differences in daily practices across cultures
Describe texture, color, and shape in artwork
Explore a variety of age-appropriate materials and media to create two-and three-dimensional artwork
Express an opinion about a work of art
Explore how color can convey mood and emotion
Play instruments using different beats, tempos, dynamics, and interpretation
Sing a variety of songs with repetitive phrases and rhythmic patterns independently and with others
Sing songs varying voice and sounds (e.g. high and low, short and long, loud and soft, or fast and slow)
Identify one source of music that can be heard in daily life
Use body, energy, space, and time to move in a few different ways
Express self freely through movement
Create characters through physical movement, gesture, sound, speech, and facial expressions
Develop audience skills by observing performances or artists at work in various aspects of the Arts

pk/language.text: Show eagerness to learn about a variety of topics and ideas
Begin to think problems through, considering several possibilities and analyzing results
Use knowledge of everyday experiences to apply to a new situation
Experiment with a variety of writing tools and surfaces
Identify story-related problems, events, and resolutions during conversations with adult
With adult assistance, retell a simple story in sequence
Identify characters and recall major events in a story
Respond appropriately to statements, questions, vocabulary, and stories
Begin to demonstrate an understanding of the differences between fantasy and reality
Know some features of a book (e.g. title, author, illustrator)
Pretend to read, using intonation and referring to images in the illustrations
Identify factual information and events during conversations with adult
Listen actively as an individual and as a member of a group to a variety of age-appropriate informational texts read aloud
Practice tracking from top to bottom and left to right with scaffolding
Identify parts of a book (e.g. front cover, back cover, spine)
Show understanding that sequence of letters represents a sequence of spoken sounds (e.g. asks how to spell a word)
With adult assistance, segment words in a simple sentence by clapping and naming number of words in a sentence
Recognize and name 10 upper-and lower-case letters
With adult assistance, generate rhyming words
Clap out the syllables in own name
With adult assistance, match the initial sound of spoken words
Associate three or more letters with their sounds
Identify some letters in own name
Recognize and “read” familiar words or environmental print
Add detail to drawings and other products with simple descriptive words, letters or letter forms
Plan and then use drawings, constructions, movements, and dramatizations to represent ideas
Tell detailed stories that refer to other times and places
Begin to use sound spelling (e.g. uses initial sound of words to write words, writes several sounds heard in words)
Recall three or four items removed from view
Listen and respond attentively to conversations (e.g. engages in at least three exchanges, poses questions and listens to the ideas of others, shares experiences when asked)
Be understood by most adults and peers
Use a variety of nouns, verbs, and descriptive phrases in meaningful contexts (vocabulary)
Use a variety of sentence structures from simple to more complex in meaningful contexts (sentence structure)
Describe and tell the use of many familiar items
With adult assistance, use word relationships to sort, classify, and serialize objects using attributes such as color, shape, or size

pk/social.text: Discuss examples of authority, rules, fairness, and personal responsibilities in own experiences and in stories read to him/her
Sometimes use appropriate social conventions in greetings, introductions, and conversations
Use turn-taking in conversations and in play
Share materials, toys, and ideas during play
Show respect and recognize the feelings of others and the causes of their reactions
Follow schedule and typical classroom routines (e.g. comes when called, sits attentively at circle, participates in clean-up)
Show satisfaction in accomplishments
Regulate emotions and begin to show self-control in handling frustration and disappointment
Express emotions through socially appropriate actions and words
Communicate personal experiences or interests
Recognize and describe own feelings
Follow routines for care of own belongings and school supplies
Sustain work on age-appropriate, interesting tasks (can ignore most distractions and interruptions)
Identify technology that can be used to gain information
